newsitem.title: USA: Great Lakes Gas line unaffected by Mich. landslide.
newsitem.headline: Great Lakes Gas line unaffected by Mich. landslide.

text.p: A landslide in the remote upper peninsula of Michigan earlier this week has not affected natural gas deliveries on Great Lakes Gas Transmission, Coastal Corp's unit ANR Pipeline said Thursday.

"There was a landslide in the upper peninsula of Michigan covering only about 15 acres of area. Sault Ste. Marie is the closest town...The pipeline has reduced operating pressure, but it is still delivering contracted volumes," the spokesman said.

A 10-12 foot section of a 10-inch diameter line, which is not part of the mainline, was exposed as a result of the landslide. The affected area is about 1.5 miles upstream of the Rudyard meter station, he added.
Great Lakes' mainline, whose primary customer is Michigan Consolidated Gas, typically has a daily throughput of about two billion cubic feet, he said.
Great Lakes is 50 percent owned by Coastal Corp and 50 percent owned by TransCanada Pipelines.
